title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp.108-109). Σ is a complete lattice with arbitrary Sup and Inf and an order-reversing involution ∁ (De Morgan). Later pages apply it to a 'spatial' Σ. Lemma 1 (p.109) takes a family e_I = (e_i), i in I, of nonzero, mutually disjoint elements with Sup_i e_i = 1. It states that two conditions are equivalent: (i) the e_i lie in a subset Σ' stable under Sup, Inf and ∁ which, with the induced structure, is a Boolean algebra; (ii) the map P(I) → Σ, J ↦ e_J = Sup_{i∈J} e_i, which always preserves Sups, also commutes with complement (∁e_J = e_{I∖J}), hence also with arbitrary Infs. The NB notes that this map is injective, with J = {i ∈ I | e_i ≤ e_J}.

This page, first part: under these conditions the image Σ_e of P(I) is the smallest subset Σ' satisfying (i). So it is the Boolean algebra generated by the e_i, and it is isomorphic to P(I).

Corollary: drop the hypothesis e := Sup e_i = 1, and adjoin e_0 := ∁e. The enlarged family ({e_i}, e_0), indexed by I ⊔ {0}, satisfies the lemma iff the following holds for every partition I = I' ⊔ I'': ∁e_{I'} = e_{I''} ∨ e_0. Applying ∁ and De Morgan, this is equivalent to e_{I'} = e ∧ ∁e_{I''}. In words, each partial join must be recoverable from the total join e by 'subtracting' the complementary partial join.

Definition: such a family is called 'admissible'. Σ_{e•} = Σ_{(e_i)} is then the Boolean algebra it generates, isomorphic to P(I ⊔ {0}).

Purpose: p.111 states the first 'axiom on the relations (rapports) in an atelier A with associated magasin F'. Atomisation 1 says that for every figure F the family (X^0)_{X∈F} in Σ_A is admissible. Grothendieck then shows the axiom is not redundant, using the atelier of finite elementary spatial figures of a spatial Σ. For two disjoint elements, admissibility reduces to: e ⊥ e' ⇒ e' = ∁e ∧ (e ∨ e'). This is exactly the orthomodular law, in its orthogonal-pair form.
errors: In the definition, 'isomorphic to P(I ⊔ {e_0})' should read P(I ⊔ {0}). It is also only correct when e_0 ≠ 0, i.e. e ≠ 1. If e = 1 then e_0 = 0, the map P(I ⊔ {0}) → Σ is not injective, and the generated algebra is P(I). The lemma's hypothesis that the elements are nonzero is thus not automatically met by e_0.

The corollary tacitly needs e_0 = ∁e to be disjoint from each e_i. That holds if ∁ is an orthocomplementation (x ∧ ∁x = 0), but not for a mere De Morgan involution. Presumably the notion of 'disjoint' in Σ (defined earlier, e.g. e ≤ ∁e') makes this automatic. Not a real gap.

The 'il faut et il suffit' is plausible but only sketched; the proof is left implicit. It is routine: necessity is immediate from (ii), and sufficiency gives ∁e_J = e_{complement of J} for all J ⊂ I ⊔ {0}.

ideas.what: Criterion for a family of pairwise disjoint elements of a complete lattice with involution to generate a Boolean subalgebra isomorphic to a power set: the join map P(I) → Σ must commute with complement.
ideas.modern_name: Boolean subalgebra generated by an orthogonal family / compatibility (commutativity) in ortholattices
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff–von Neumann (1936); Husimi (1937); Foulis, Kalmbach (orthomodular lattice theory, 1960s–80s)

ideas.what: Admissibility condition: for every partition I = I' ⊔ I'', e_{I'} = e ∧ ∁e_{I''} (with e = Sup e_i). In the two-element case this is e ⊥ e' ⇒ e' = ∁e ∧ (e ∨ e').
ideas.modern_name: orthomodular law (orthogonal form): a ⊥ b ⇒ b = (a ∨ b) ∧ a^⊥

ideas.what: Using this admissibility as an axiom ('Atomisation 1') on the lattice Σ_A of an 'atelier' with its 'magasin' of figures (next page).
ideas.modern_name: no standard modern counterpart; resembles axioms for orthomodular / test-space structures (Foulis–Randall)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's admissibility axiom for ateliers is, in the two-element case, exactly the orthomodular law of quantum logic. His 'atomisation' axiom thus requires figures to behave like orthogonal decompositions in an orthomodular lattice, a link to Foulis–Randall test spaces and quantum logic that he does not name.
missed.quote: on ait ∁e_{I'} = e_{I''} ∨ e_0 ou ce qui revient au même (passant aux ∁) e_{I'} = e ∧ ∁e_{I''}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It places the unpublished 1986 'ateliers' theory relative to known lattice theory. This is useful for anyone reconstructing that theory; the lattice-theoretic content itself is classical.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is a routine lattice-theoretic lemma, essentially a rediscovery of the orthomodular law and of Boolean subalgebras generated by orthogonal families. Its only interest is as part of the unpublished 'ateliers' axiomatics.
transcription_corrections: 'isom. à 𝔓(I ⊔ {e_0})' — the image reads roughly '∏(I ⊔ {e_0})' / P(I ⊔ {e_0}); mathematically it should be P(I ⊔ {0}).
'il faut et il suffit [?] que' — the image shows 'il f[au]t' at the line end and '& que' on the next line, consistent with 'il faut et il suffit que'.
'Pour que les conditions des lemmes soient satisfaites' is probably 'du lemme' (singular, Lemma 1).
